newsitem.title: DUBAI: Dubai formalises foreign bank tax code.
newsitem.headline: Dubai formalises foreign bank tax code.

text.p: United Arab Emirates' member Dubai has formalised rules requiring foreign banks operating in the emirate to pay 20 percent tax, bankers said on Sunday.
"The authorities have codified the tax rules," the head of finance at a large overseas bank said.
"It's business as usual. This just formalises prior agreements with individual banks," said the financial controller of a foreign bank dominant in the Dubai market.

They were referring to a circular sent out last week by Deputy Ruler of Dubai Sheikh Hamdan bin Rashid al-Maktoum regulating the assessment of tax on foreign bank branches, which bankers said had long been subject to the tax.

The foreign bank branch must pay the tax by the end of March -- three months after the end of the financial year. If it fails to pay by then, a fine of one percent of the amount owed will be levied for every month that it is overdue.
There are 27 foreign banks, 15 representative offices and 19 local banks operating in the UAE.
Lawyers said foreign banks in the other two main emirates -- Abu Dhabi and Sharjah -- are subject to similar taxes.
